text:
release-bot: Deploy v2026.03.14 -> canary (us-west-2) finished. traffic=5%. Initial smoke checks passed, but we are seeing a spike in 5xx/error-rate for the canary group.

incident-bot: PagerDuty incident triggered: INC-7842 — canary-error-rate-high (p95 latency and 5xx spike) — paging on-call.

sophie: Acking. I'm on it. Jamal, you're primary for runtime today. Can everyone drop what they're doing and join triage in this thread? :eyes:

jamal: looking now. Grafana shows p95 latency jumped to ~4.8s and 5xx =~5% for canary. Errors correlate with the embedder sidecar returning 502s.

devon: scanning logs — I see repeated lines like: `runtime/kern_quant: allocation failed, falling back` and then the sidecar returning 502. Possibly the new quant kernel path hitting a mem cap.

luis: quick idea — either reduce canary traffic to 0% or switch canary to fallback model variant (non-quant) while we triage. Which is faster?

sophie: we should cut canary traffic first to stop customer impact. If rollback is safe, do that too. Jamal, reduce to 1% now, then 0%. Provide commands if you need help.

jamal: reducing traffic to 1%. running:
```
redwood traffic set --release v2026.03.14 --canary 1 --region us-west-2
```

jamal: setting to 0% now.
```
redwood traffic set --release v2026.03.14 --canary 0 --region us-west-2
```

jamal: confirmed: canary traffic = 0%. Metrics starting to fall.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-7842 acknowledged by sophie. If not resolved, will escalate to secondary in 8m.

devon: I can reproduce a local stress test hitting the quant path and getting OOM-ish allocation failures on the new kernel. Looks like a subset of GPUs with a driver/kern combo.

luis: if we want to rollback instead of just cutting traffic, command is:
```
redwood rollout rollback --release v2026.03.14 --to v2026.03.13 --regions us-west-2
```
Which will revert the canary and update global if we choose.

sophie: let's roll back to v2026.03.13 for the affected region and keep monitoring. Jamal, initiate rollback and monitor healthchecks. Devon, start root cause triage on kernel/quant interplay.

jamal: initiating rollback now. output: `rollback job started, id=rb-9021`. Watching healthchecks.

release-bot: Rollback job rb-9021: staging->us-west-2: tasks scheduled.

jamal: rollback complete in us-west-2, healthchecks green. p95 back to baseline within ~2m. 5xx rates returned to normal.

emily (support): quick customer-impact note: only canary (5% -> 0%) saw elevated 5xx for ~6 minutes. Estimated affected sessions ~0.9% of total active requests in us-west-2. No major customers reported; support on standby. Recommend no external comms unless we see >2% of prod impacted.

devon: logging a follow-up ticket with diagnostics and the minimal repro. Hypothesis: kernel selector didn't gate fallback for certain quant layouts, causing allocation regression under specific request shapes.

luis: filing PR to add a conservative fallback flag and a runtime guard for the quant path.

sophie: good — assign postmortem to devon, remediation tasks to luis. We'll keep the incident open for monitoring for 30m, then resolve if stable. Thanks for the quick action everyone. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: PagerDuty incident INC-7842 marked as resolved by jamal at 4267890395. Tags: rollback, canary, kernel-quant. Postmortem assigned.

sophie: short follow-up actions — (1) schedule a kernel/quant review with runtime team tomorrow, (2) add rollback gating to release playbook, (3) add alert tweak so canary errors >1% triggers earlier NOC page.

jamal: copied. monitoring alert config change queued.

devon: will own RC for the fix and draft the postmortem.

luis: PR incoming for guardrail flag.

sophie: closing thread once monitoring window passed. Thanks all.
